name: Ahasuerus
bio: Ahasuerus, king of Persia, ruled from India to Ethiopia over 127 provinces from his palace in Susa. In the third year of his reign, he threw a lavish 180-day banquet for his nobles and officials, followed by a seven-day feast for everyone in Susa, while Queen Vashti held a separate feast for the women. On the seventh day, drunk and wanting to display Vashti's beauty, he summoned her before his guests; when she refused to come, he grew furious and, on his advisor Memucan's counsel, issued an irrevocable decree deposing her as queen and barring her from his presence (Esther 1:1-22). His search for a new queen — which brings Esther to his court — is told in detail in the chapters ahead. Ahasuerus later promoted Haman the Agagite above all his other officials; when Haman asked for authority to destroy the empire's Jews over their supposed disobedience to royal law, the king gave him his signet ring and let him proceed, unaware this would target his own queen's people (Esther 3:1, 8-11). Unable to sleep one night, Ahasuerus had the court chronicles read to him and learned Mordecai had never been honored for exposing the chamberlains' assassination plot; when Haman unwittingly described his own enemy's reward, the king had him bestow it on Mordecai instead of executing him (Esther 6:1-11).
